question: How do advanced software engineering organizations (Google SRE, AWS, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic MCP, Netflix, Palantir Foundry) implement multi-strategy deliberation, 18-dimensional decision scoring, decision transparency, engineering economics, and performance memory tracking without vendor lock-in?
scope: Multi-candidate strategy generation, decision optimization across 18 dimensions, decision transparency logging (WHY_SELECTED vs WHY_REJECTED), provider-neutral engineering economics, and synthetic agent/tool performance memory
claims: Evaluating multiple candidate strategies before execution prevents local optima traps and enforces evidence-backed decision quality.
Decision transparency requires explicitly auditing why a winning strategy was selected AND why non-winning candidates were rejected.
evidence: AWS Step Functions and Netflix Conductor evaluate parallel workflow paths before selecting optimal execution routes.
Palantir Foundry tracks asset line-of-sight metrics to balance analytical execution cost against data accuracy.
observations: Initial scoring weights for multi-dimensional evaluation must be explicitly flagged as ASSUMPTION until empirical telemetry is collected.
Synthetic performance tracking for tools and agents must remain strictly distinguished from production empirical metrics.
limitations: Strategy simulation operates via synthetic mock models prior to live production API integration.
recommendation: Implement Engineering Factory Strategy Engine, 18-dimensional Strategy Selection Engine, Decision Transparency Logging, Engineering Economics Model, and Performance Memory Registries in EOS Control Plane.
